name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Rupiah holds near record lows around 18,200 per dollar after Bank Indonesia's rate rises; no EM default or IMF rescue
state: The rupiah traded near 18,200 per dollar in mid-November, close to its record low of about 18,280, with outflows expected from MSCI index changes effective 30 Nov; Bank Indonesia has raised rates by 125bp since May to 6% (Trading Economics). The fall has been gradual, short of 10% in a month. No major emerging economy in default, imposing capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 26 Nov, so the level stays Normal.
for_you: People in economies with weakening currencies face higher import prices, and firms with dollar debts face higher repayment costs.
rubric_hit: No major EM currency down >10% in a month, no default or IMF emergency request = Normal

sources.title: Trading Economics — Rupiah recovers but heads for weekly losses
FXStreet — Indonesian rupiah gains on easing political uncertainty despite MSCI outflow risks

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
